rounds.name: Worker-Greer
rounds.text:
If I withhold pay, the worker still wants to avoid a penalty and will tend to do the job properly to earn the extra tasks, giving me the higher payoff (5 vs 1). Trusting gives them a free ride to cut corners, risking zero tasks. Hence withholding dominates.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Greer
rounds.text:
Withholding pay always yields at least as many completed tasks as trusting, and strictly more in both possible worker behaviors (5 vs 3 if they work properly, 1 vs 0 if they cut corners). Thus it dominates trust.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Greer
rounds.text:
Withholding pay gives the worker a stronger incentive to complete the job properly, guaranteeing at least 5 tasks if they comply and still yields 1 task even if they cut corners. Trust offers a chance of zero tasks if they cut corners, making it riskier.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Greer
rounds.text:
Withholding pay gives higher rewards whether the worker does the job properly (5 vs 3) or cuts corners (1 vs 0), and it also discourages corner‑cutting. Even accounting for the occasional technical failure, it dominates TRUST.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Greer
rounds.text:
Withholding pay gives a higher payoff no matter whether the worker does the job properly or cuts corners (5 vs 3 and 1 vs 0). Since we want to maximize completed tasks, the safe dominant choice is to withhold.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Greer
rounds.text:
Choosing WITHHOLD always yields at least as many completed tasks as TRUST, and strictly more in both possible worker behaviors.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Greer
rounds.text:
If I trust, the worker can safely cut corners and give me nothing, whereas withholding gives me at least one completed task even if they cut. Since I don’t know the worker’s intent, the safe choice is to withhold pay and still get some work done.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Greer
rounds.text:
Withholding pay always yields at least as many completed tasks as trusting, and often more, regardless of whether the worker cuts corners or not. Therefore the safest choice for maximizing tasks is to withhold.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Greer
rounds.text:
Withholding pay gives the worker a strong incentive to do the job properly (5 tasks versus only 3 when trusted) and still yields a positive outcome even if they cut corners. Since we want to maximize expected completed tasks, the safest high‑payoff choice is to withhold.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Greer
rounds.text:
Choosing WITHHOLD gives at least 1 completed task even if the worker cuts corners, and yields 5 tasks when they work properly, which is strictly better than the maximum 3 tasks possible with TRUST. Hence, withholding pay dominates trusting.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD
